newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Labor Secy Reich urges care in adjusting CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Labor Secy Reich urges care in adjusting CPI.

text.p: The government must be careful about altering the consumer price index in a bid to save money on cost of living increases for pensioners, veterans and other beneficiaries, Labor Secretary Robert Reich said on Tuesday.
"We've got to be careful," he told CNN television. "We do want to have cost-of-living increases" for those beneficiaries.
A congressionally appointed panel is scheduled to release a report on Wednesday stating that the consumer price index (CPI) overstates inflation by a percentage point or more.

Some Republican and Democratic lawmakers have argued that cost of living increases for Social Security pensioners and other government beneficiaries -- which are tied to the CPI -- should be reduced accordingly. That would save the government billions of dollars and help balance the budget.
But the Clinton administration has resisted that, saying that any changes in the consumer price index should be made by government statisticians, not by politicians.
Reich hewed to that line on Tuesday. "It must not become a political football," he said. "We've got to keep it strictly technical."
